### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
The driver chooses the time step, executes every stage, checks rejection, and writes accepted states.
Caller supplied; integration defaults belong to pyharp.
Order: code map; no independent measured convergence order.
No defining equation: this section maps control flow or data ownership.
:::

The driver chooses the time step, executes every stage, checks rejection, and writes accepted states. There is no main
time loop inside a MeshBlock. The C++ example applies kinetics after all dynamics stages and before the rejection
decision.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The driver keeps the clock unchanged when a step is rejected. A positive return from `check_redo` repeats the cycle; a
negative return ends it. `max_time_step` first reduces the local hydro limit with MIN, then applies the Courant factor
and the redo halving. Outputs are scheduled after the accepted clock increment. The `straka` driver also writes
immediately after initialization, including restart. No independent spatial or temporal order belongs to this control
flow; it inherits the selected operators.

### Limits

The restart writer saves output counters before `make_outputs` increments them. Together with the unconditional
initial output in `straka`, this is a code-level reason to investigate repeated restart outputs; no overwrite
experiment is reported here. Driver-split kinetics is outside the MeshBlock stage.
